statement: Whiskering defines functors $\mathcal T(\tau,\tau^{\prime})\to\operatorname{Fun}(P_{\tau^{\prime}}(X),P_\tau(X))$ and the corresponding functor with fixed endpoints, where $\mathcal T$ is the endpoint-preserving type-map category.
repair: For $\eta:\varphi\Rightarrow\psi$, send $F$ to $F\eta$; fullness of permitted-path categories and the interchange law verify the claim. Commentary: Why a homotopy of types acts on every path.
notes: This asserts functorial dependence on transformations of type maps, not equivalence of each pullback functor.

statement: $\Sigma_\tau$ consists of the identities and the backward arrows of $I_\tau$; it is closed under composition.
repair: Backward composable arrows lie in one backward-oriented run; their composite is backward. Interval categories have no nonidentity isomorphisms.

statement: For marked categories $(I,\Sigma_I),(I^{\prime},\Sigma_{I^{\prime}}),(X,\Sigma)$, composition restricts to a functor between the full subcategories of marking-preserving functors.
repair: The composite preserves markings, and all natural transformations between allowed objects remain available.
notes: No condition that components of natural transformations lie in the markings is imposed.

statement: A type map $\varphi:I_\tau\to I_{\tau^{\prime}}$ sends every backward arrow to a backward arrow or an identity.
repair: Its vertex map is monotone for the geometric order; a backward directed edge can therefore only traverse a backward-oriented run or collapse.
references: GrothendieckDerivateursVII, VII §6; index_earlier.md, DER_VII-a, A morphism is a list of increments

statement: The whiskering action is over $X\times X$, and its natural transformations are vertical; hence it restricts to every fixed-endpoint path category.
repair: Endpoint components of every type-map transformation are identities, so whiskering preserves the strict fibre at $(a,b)$.
notes: The words over X on p.97 are a slip for over X×X, already made clear by the diagram.

statement: If two type maps are joined by a finite zigzag of transformations, their induced pullback functors on permitted paths are joined by a finite zigzag, also with fixed endpoints.
repair: Apply the functor on hom-categories to each arrow of the zigzag.

statement: For $\operatorname{Hom}_{Ty}(\tau,\tau^{\prime})\ne\varnothing$, all induced pullback functors $P_{\tau^{\prime}}(X)\to P_\tau(X)$ have the same class in $\mathrm{Cat\,hot}$, and likewise with fixed endpoints.
repair: Combines the interval homotopy lemma of §8 with whiskering.
notes: The assertion is independence from a choice of parallel map, not that a type change is a weak equivalence.

statement: The preceding equality can be taken in the homotopy category of categories over $X\times X$, using vertical transformations.
repair: The endpoint-fixed action supplies the strengthened relative statement; the fibre theorem is then its direct corollary.

statement: For a Grothendieck fibration $C\to T$, assume that pullbacks along any two arrows with the same source and target are joined by finite zigzags of natural transformations.
notes: Called the homotopy hypothesis. It is proved for the motivating path fibration in §9.

statement: $P=T_o$ is the thin category on $\operatorname{Ob}T$ with $t\le t^{\prime}$ iff $\operatorname{Hom}_T(t,t^{\prime})$ is nonempty.
notes: It is a preorder, not necessarily an antisymmetric poset; the edition explicitly allows nonidentity isomorphisms.

statement: The identity-on-objects functor $q:T\to P$ is universal among functors constant on each hom-set, in particular among functors to thin categories.
repair: Define the image of the unique arrow in P by the common value of the arrows of T; composition and uniqueness follow immediately.
notes: The manuscript parenthesis equating thinness with all arrows being monomorphisms is false and is corrected in the edition.

statement: The homotopy hypothesis is equivalent to factorization of $T^{op}\to\mathrm{Cat\,hot}$ through $P^{op}$; the factor is uniquely determined.
repair: The preceding universal property applies. A cleavage only produces pseudofunctorial comparison isomorphisms before passing to Cat hot, where these become equalities.

statement: Assume $P$ is nonempty and any two objects have a common lower bound.
gap_or_error: The displayed pairwise condition alone does not imply nonemptiness.
repair: Read nonemptiness as part of the conventional word filtrant, as in Stacks Project Definition 4.19.1; do not allow the empty-base vacuity.

statement: The preorder of $Ty$ satisfies the preceding condition: $\tau\tau^{\prime}$ maps to both factors by collapsing the other factor to the terminal empty type.
repair: Use $\operatorname{id}_\tau*p_{\tau^{\prime}}$ and $p_\tau*\operatorname{id}_{\tau^{\prime}}$; the empty type supplies a base object.

statement: The filtered diagram $H_C:P^{op}\to\mathrm{Cat\,hot}$ defines an ind-object of $\mathrm{Cat\,hot}$.
notes: Its image in Ind Hot is obtained by applying the nerve-homotopy localization levelwise.

statement: Assume that $P$ has a countable left-cofinal family; this holds in particular if its object set is countable.
repair: For the implication in parentheses, enumerate all objects; nonemptiness has already been included in filtration.

statement: A countable cofinal family in a nonempty downward-directed preorder can be replaced by a decreasing cofinal sequence $t_0\leftarrow t_1\leftarrow\cdots$ of actual arrows in $T$.
repair: Enumerate $s_n$ and choose $t_{n+1}$ below both $t_n$ and $s_{n+1}$, then choose a witnessing arrow to $t_n$. Commentary: Making a sequence strict.

statement: A split fibration is one obtained from a strict functor $T^{op}\to\mathrm{Cat}$, so that the selected pullbacks preserve composition and identities strictly.
Every Grothendieck fibration is equivalent over its base to a split fibration.
repair: Giraud splitting; a concrete right splitting uses cartesian functors $T/t\to C$, whose evaluation at $\operatorname{id}_t$ is equivalent to the fibre. Modern precise reference: Emmenegger et al., Theorem 5.4 and Remark 5.5.
references: EmmeneggerMesitiRosoliniStreicher2024, Theorem 5.4 and Remark 5.5; SGA1, Exposé VI §§8–9
notes: An equivalent replacement is allowed; the same underlying fibration need not itself admit a splitting.

statement: The pullbacks along a chosen decreasing chain give a sequential direct system $C_n=C_{t_n}$ whose image in Ind Cat hot is $H_C$.
repair: Define long transitions as composites of adjacent transitions, even without a globally split cleavage; cofinality in P proves equality of the represented ind-object.

statement: $C_\infty=\operatorname{colim}_n C_n$ is the ordinary filtered colimit of the sequential category diagram.
notes: It must be distinguished from the total category and from the formal ind-object.

statement: The displayed transition $C_{t_n}\to C_{t_{n-1}}$ has the variance required by the sequential direct system.
gap_or_error: The arrow is reversed in the edition itself, not in the transcription.
repair: The intended transition is $C_{t_{n-1}}\to C_{t_n}$, induced by $t_n\to t_{n-1}$.
notes: PDF leaf33 visibly confirms the reversed printed arrow; retained in source and registered as edition slip.

statement: If all direct-system transitions are fully faithful, each $C_n\to C_\infty$ is fully faithful; if they are also injective on objects, the stages can be realized as full subcategories of the colimit.
repair: Hom-sets between representatives at one stage are unchanged at later stages. Objectwise injectivity gives literal inclusions; without it the assertion is an embedding up to equivalence.

statement: Compare the total category $C$, the various sequential colimits $C_\infty$, and the ind-object $H_C$, in Cat hot and in Hot; determine dependence on the chosen cofinal chain.
repair: General total-versus-colimit equivalence fails by the one-object group example on p.109. Noncanonical independence of sequential models in Hot follows by interleaving cofinal chains and comparing telescopes; commentary Independence of the sequential homotopy type. This does not produce a Cat-hot equivalence or a preferred Hot isomorphism.
notes: Open describes the source at this point, not contemporary mathematical status.

statement: Restriction of $H_C$ to a left-cofinal full subpreorder of $P$ represents the same ind-object.
repair: The inclusion of a nonempty left-cofinal full subpreorder of a cofiltered preorder is cofinal; the ind-Hom formula is unchanged.
notes: The accompanying assertion that sequential models are unchanged is justified up to noncanonical Hot isomorphism by the interleaving proof; literal isomorphism of the chosen ordinary categories is not asserted.

statement: The thin reflection of the slice satisfies $(T/t_0)_o=P/t_0=\{t:t\le t_0\}$.
gap_or_error: Slice objects retain a chosen arrow to $t_0$, and the preorder relation also depends on its commutative triangle. Thin reflection does not commute with this slice.
repair: Use the full subcategory on objects admitting some arrow to $t_0$, whose preorder is the lower ideal, or impose actual categorical cofiltering on T for a valid slice-cofinality argument. Full counterexample and repairs in A slice does not have the same preorder.
notes: Walking parallel pair $s\rightrightarrows t_0$: P has a least object but the slice has two incomparable minimal objects. Even skeletal reflection does not fix the equality.

statement: Under only the stated preorder filtration, passage from $T$ to $T/t_0$ automatically gives another filtered indexing preorder and leaves the same ind-object construction available.
gap_or_error: The slice preorder need not be cofiltered; the preceding walking-parallel-pair example is a counterexample.
repair: Restriction to the full lower-ideal subcategory works under the stated hypotheses. For the actual slice, require additional parallel-arrow equalization, e.g. T cofiltered. Do not infer slice filtration merely from objectwise lower bounds.

statement: If the total category were canonically recovered from the ind-object, restriction to a preorder-cofinal chain would preserve its homotopy type.
repair: The conditional is correct, but its premise fails for the general fibred situation. The group-base example identifies the missing higher base information.
notes: Exploratory consequence, not a proof of invariance.

statement: For a left-cofinal base change $\alpha:T^{\prime}\to T$ preserving the indicated ind-diagram, is $C\times_TT^{\prime}\to C$ a Cat-hot isomorphism or at least a weak equivalence of nerves?
repair: Preorder cofinality does not suffice. If every comma category $\alpha/t$ has contractible nerve, the projection is a weak equivalence for every Grothendieck fibration, by cartesian lifting and Quillen A; this condition is also necessary for that universal conclusion.
references: Lurie2009HTT, Corollary 4.1.3.3; commentary The cofinality condition that controls total categories
notes: The source uses cofinality at the preorder level in its sequential construction. Stronger homotopy cofinality must be distinguished.

statement: $\mathcal H_T(S_T,C)$ is the Grothendieck fibration associated to $t\mapsto\operatorname{Fun}(S,C_t)$.
notes: Its total category differs from the ordinary functor category Fun(S,C).

statement: The preceding fibrewise functor category can be interpreted as the internal morphism object between the associated category-valued stacks over the presheaf topos $\widehat T$.
gap_or_error: The text suppresses the extension from T to its presheaf topos and the topology used on that topos.
repair: Use the canonical topology on the presheaf topos and extend a fibred category by cartesian sections over categories of elements. The statement is about stacks in categories, not only groupoid-valued stacks.
notes: No further use of this optional stack interpretation is required for any proof in this chunk.

statement: The homotopy hypothesis is preserved on replacing $C_t$ by $\operatorname{Fun}(S,C_t)$ for any small S.
repair: Postcomposition sends each natural transformation of reindexing functors to a natural transformation on these functor categories, and therefore preserves finite zigzags.

statement: $H(S)=\pi_0\mathcal H_T(S_T,C)$ is a contravariant functor of S and is naturally $\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Ind}(\mathrm{Cat\,hot})}(S,H_C)$.
repair: Connected components of a Grothendieck construction equal the colimit of the fibre component sets; the homotopy hypothesis factors this diagram through P. Full proof in The functor represented by the ind-object.
notes: Introduced hypothetically, then asserted later on p.106; source proof_status stated records the final stance on the same page.

statement: The functor $S\mapsto H(S)$ determines $H_C$ up to unique isomorphism as an ind-object.
repair: The standard embedding of Ind(Cat hot) in set-valued presheaves on Cat hot is fully faithful; the preceding formula identifies its image.
notes: Uniqueness here refers to the representing ind-object with its representing isomorphism, not to arbitrary isomorphisms between bare homotopy types.

statement: $\pi_0C\cong\pi_0 C_\infty\cong\operatorname{colim}_{P^{op}}\pi_0C_t$.
repair: Apply the Grothendieck component formula and the sequential cofinality argument; pi0 commutes with ordinary colimits. The full proof is included in The functor represented by the ind-object.

statement: For a category S with finitely many objects and arrows, $H(S)\cong\mathrm{Cat\,hot}(S,C_\infty)$.
repair: A functor, natural transformation, or finite zigzag from finite S uses finitely many data and equations, which descend simultaneously to one stage. Full proof and an infinite-discrete-source counterexample are given in the commentary.
notes: The finiteness condition is categorical finite presentation; it is not finite-dimensionality of the nerve.

statement: With an additional sufficiently strong comparison hypothesis, the formulas involving Cat hot can be expressed with Hot instead.
gap_or_error: No precise additional hypothesis is specified here; this is not an unconditional theorem.
repair: State the required comparison bijections for the chosen probes and stages, or use compact homotopy probes when commuting maps with filtered homotopy colimits. A finite category alone is insufficient; the B(C2) skeleton example in the commentary gives a counterexample to that stronger assertion.

statement: Are the sets $\mathrm{Cat\,hot}(S,C)$ or $\mathrm{Hot}(S,C)$ naturally identified with $H(S)$ beyond S=e?
repair: No in the stated generality: for C=T=B(C2), H(S) is a singleton for every S while S=B(C2) has distinct trivial and identity maps into C, in both homotopy categories. Full calculation in What a one-object base can retain.

statement: An isomorphism on the preceding component sets need not extend to higher homotopy groups or to a Hot equivalence of the compared objects.
repair: Confirmed in the abstract setting by the group-base example on p.109; it must not be read as a counterexample for the special path fibration.
notes: The later all-arrows path comparison in §13 has the opposite outcome.

statement: The canonical span is $C\leftarrow E=C\times_T\mathbf N^{op}\xrightarrow{q}C_\infty$, and q inverts cartesian transport arrows.
repair: The functor sends a stage object or arrow to its filtered-colimit class; a cartesian transition has identity image.
notes: This is a localization up to categorical equivalence. A strict localization with unchanged object set is not claimed by the useful version of the assertion.

statement: For every sequence of small categories, $q:\int_{\mathbf N^{op}}C_n\to\operatorname{colim}_n C_n$ is a weak equivalence of nerves.
repair: Thomason identifies the total category with the homotopy colimit; nerve commutes with filtered colimits, and filtered homotopy colimits of simplicial sets map by weak equivalences to ordinary colimits. The commentary supplies the representative-category proof of the last step.

statement: The span defines a morphism $C_\infty\to C$ in Hot by inverting q.
repair: Compose the inverse of [q] with the projection [E→C].
notes: A choice of cofinal chain is still part of the displayed construction.

statement: Preorder filtration and countable cofinality do not force $C_\infty\to C$ to be a weak equivalence, even with the homotopy hypothesis.
repair: Take C=T=BG for a nontrivial group: all fibres and the sequential colimit are terminal, while the total category has fundamental group G. The manuscript gives the one-object warning; the commentary works it out.

statement: The underlying total category need not be determined by the ind-object constructed after passing to the preorder.
repair: The total category can retain the homotopy of the base; constant fibrations have total space BT×BD and ind-object constant at D.
notes: The accompanying phrase that the bare category has no interesting geometry is a methodological judgement, not a mathematical theorem. Its valid content is failure of determination by H_C.

statement: A natural equivalence $C_\infty\simeq C$ would provide a way to compare choices and transport the total path composition to the sequential model.
repair: Correct once naturality and the comparison maps are specified; a bare existence of some isomorphism does not imply unique comparison isomorphisms. The equivalence transports composition in Hot, without automatically producing a strict composition functor on the chosen category C_infty.
notes: The subsequent source retracts the proposed obstruction. Section 13 gives the positive unrestricted path comparison; its constant-path lemma is left unwritten at p.170 and proved in the status commentary.

statement: Concatenation on the total path categories is a strictly associative and unital functor.
repair: Established in §7 and its functorial verification on pp.77–82; componentwise concatenation of transformations proves associativity.
notes: This is a recall, not a new gap.

statement: The chosen sequential presentation does not by itself provide an evident strictly natural concatenation functor on its ordinary colimit; the ind-object carries the intended operation.
repair: A coherent multiplicative model or suitable additional comparisons are needed for strict descent. This is a statement about this chosen presentation, not nonexistence of strict loop-space models.
notes: The invalid strictification obstruction on p.113 is audited separately.

statement: The comparison is claimed to hold if $T\to P$ is smooth and coaspherical, or proper and aspherical, in the terminology of earlier chapters.
gap_or_error: No proof or explicit reduction to the earlier base-change criteria is given on these pages.
repair: Proved in “Why the smooth and proper criteria suffice”. The fibre criterion and added coasphericity/asphericity make each strict fibre contractible. The homotopy hypothesis makes its coefficient diagram locally constant. Pointwise left homotopy Kan extension in the smooth case has an invertible unit; pointwise right extension in the proper case has an invertible counit. Homotopy finality of the selected sequence in the preorder then proves that the canonical comparison is a weak equivalence.
references: Maltsiniotis2005Asphericite, Theorem 1.2(b), printed p.4, and smooth/proper duality pp.4–5; Cisinski2009LocallyConstant, Proposition 1.14 and Corollary 1.18, printed pp.598–599, and their duals; Thomason1979, Theorem 1.2
notes: The criterion uses the source hypothesis on parallel pullbacks. It does not imply the universal comma criterion for all fibrations; the absorbing-zero monoid example in the proof makes this distinction explicit. Source proof_status remains stated.

statement: If T itself is the cofiltered preorder P, the comparison $C_\infty\to C$ is a weak equivalence.
repair: For the chosen decreasing cofinal chain, each comma category alpha/t is a nonempty tail of N^op with a terminal object; cartesian lifting and the dual of Quillen A make the vertical map of the span a weak equivalence, as is q.
references: Lurie2009HTT, Corollary 4.1.3.3, applied to the opposite functor; commentary The cofinality condition that controls total categories
notes: This abstract preorder case is proved independently of the later path comparison; source proof_status remains stated.

statement: The functor $Ty\to Ty_o$ is neither 0-proper nor 0-smooth in the inherited terminology.
gap_or_error: No proof is given here, and this is not a consequence merely of the existence of parallel arrows.
repair: Proved in the commentary block “Two disconnected lifting categories”: the smooth lifting category for b=+-+ and a=+ has two isolated objects, as does the proper lifting category for a=++ and b=+. The connected-lift criterion applies by the cited theorem with W=W_0. The unrestricted path-category comparison receives a separate positive argument in §13; see VIIb-C053.
references: Maltsiniotis2005Asphericite, Theorem 1.2(b), printed p.4, and its dual; GrothendieckDerivateursVII, VII p.112 and §13
notes: Source proof_status remains stated; the present commentary verifies the assertion using explicit witnesses and the historical connected-lifting interpretation.

statement: For the motivating path fibration, Grothendieck suspects that $C_\infty\to C$ is generally not a Hot isomorphism.
repair: The proposed obstruction is retracted in footnote24. For Sigma=all arrows, §13, pp.157–170, gives the positive comparison through the two Grothendieck-construction projections and their fixed-endpoint fibres. The constant-path lemma X→Fun(I_tau,X), stated on p.160, is left without a written proof on p.170; the status commentary supplies its elementary contraction proof.
notes: This is a temporary source conjecture, not an open present-day problem for unrestricted paths. The unwritten lemma is not a sequential-colimit lemma: p.159 recalls that comparison as already checked. No assertion for arbitrary Sigma follows without a separate argument.

statement: A loop-space multiplication cannot in general be represented by a strictly associative simplicial monoid, so such strict multiplication would obstruct the proposed comparison.
gap_or_error: The purported obstruction is false even for simplicial groups. The source explicitly retracts it in footnote24.
repair: Kan loop groups model the loop space of a reduced simplicial set, with strictly associative multiplication. Stevenson, arXiv:1112.0474v2, Theorem21 gives a checked modern proof of the unit equivalence.
references: Stevenson2012, Theorem 21; GrothendieckDerivateursVII, VII p.113 footnote24

statement: For a pointed connected simplicial homotopy type, a reduced simplicial model X has a simplicial loop group GX with $X\simeq\overline W GX$.
repair: Kan loop-group theorem; reduce to the basepoint component and a one-vertex model. This verifies the footnote correction.

statement: There is a natural morphism from the ind-object H_C to the constant ind-object C_infty, after the chosen cofinal chain is fixed.
repair: For each t choose t_n→t, form C_t→C_tn→C_infty, and use the homotopy hypothesis plus eventual domination to show independence in Cat hot. These classes are compatible and define the ind-morphism.

statement: The cocones to C and C_infty, together with $C_\infty\to C$ in Hot, give the displayed commuting diagram in Ind Hot.
repair: Cartesian lifts give natural transformations between the fibre inclusions and their reindexed versions, so the cocone is compatible in Cat hot; the sequential span then gives commutativity in Ind Hot.
notes: The arrow C_infty→C need not be an isomorphism in the abstract situation.

statement: The image of C_infty in the presheaf category on finite homotopy probes is canonically the filtered colimit of the image of H_C.
repair: For a finite CW homotopy type K, maps from K commute with filtered homotopy colimits. Apply the sequential total-versus-colimit equivalence. The relevant probes have the homotopy type of finite CW complexes; a finite category need not supply such a probe.
notes: Restricted-Yoneda uniqueness is weaker than a claim of a unique isomorphism between the underlying objects of Hot.

statement: Concatenation gives functors $P_\tau(a,b)\times P_{\tau^{\prime}}(b,c)\to P_{\tau\tau^{\prime}}(a,c)$.
repair: Recalled from the functorial concatenation already proved in §7.

statement: For an arbitrary chosen cofinal sequence of types, concatenation has target stage n+m: $P_{t_n}(a,b)\times P_{t_m}(b,c)\to P_{t_{n+m}}(a,c)$.
gap_or_error: The claimed indexing requires a multiplicative standard sequence, or specified maps $t_{n+m}\to t_nt_m$; cofinality alone does not supply them.
repair: For a general sequence choose a sufficiently large k(n,m) and a map t_k→t_nt_m. Alternatively choose t_n=(Delta_+Delta_-)^n. The slow cofinal sequence in The stage of a concatenation gives a complete counterexample to the unqualified n+m formula.
notes: This is a local missing convention, not a failure of the ind-object multiplication.

statement: The fibre concatenations are compatible with reindexing up to functorial homotopy, and therefore induce associative unital pairings of ind-objects.
repair: Pass to Cat hot, where the parallel-operation theorem makes the needed diagrams commute; concatenate types and then choose cofinal stages. Associativity is checked before passing to the ind-category.
references: GrothendieckDerivateursVII, VII §§7 and 9; commentary Parameters turn the ind-object back into localization

statement: If Sigma is all arrows, reversal induces ind-morphisms H_T(a,b)→H_T(b,a) satisfying the inverse identities for concatenation.
repair: The backtracking contractions in §7 are natural for parameterized families; evaluate on every Y and use Yoneda in Ind Cat hot.
notes: For a general relative class Sigma, reversal of a permitted path need not be permitted; only the category structure remains.

statement: For any object Y of Ind Cat hot, the sets $H_T^Y(a,b)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Ind}(\mathrm{Cat\,hot})}(Y,H_T(a,b))$ form the hom-sets of a category with objects Ob X; it is a groupoid if Sigma is all arrows.
repair: Apply Hom(Y,-) to the ind-composition, units, and when applicable inverse maps.
notes: The printed ambient Hom_Cat hot is an abuse; H_T is an ind-object.

statement: For an actual small category Y, X(Y)=Fun(Y,X) and Sigma_Y is the class of componentwise-Sigma natural transformations.
repair: Identities and composites are componentwise, so Sigma_Y is admissible.

statement: For every small category Y, $H_T^Y(a,b)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X(Y)[\Sigma_Y^{-1}]}(a_Y,b_Y)$, compatibly with concatenation and identity.
repair: Exchange the Y and interval variables to identify Fun(Y,P_tau(X;a,b)) with the fixed-type Sigma_Y paths in Fun(Y,X). Apply §7 localization and the component/ind-Hom formula. Full proof in Parameters turn the ind-object back into localization.
notes: The printed left side on p.117 omits Y. For Y formal ind, replace the right side by an inverse limit over a presentation; do not form Fun(Y,X) without a separate definition.

statement: In the geometric path case, different cofinal sequences yield C_infty with the same weak homotopy type, although a canonical comparison is not established here.
repair: Interleave two cofinal chains and compare their telescopes, using homotopic bonding maps. The commentary proves this noncanonical Hot independence under the abstract homotopy hypothesis for any two cofinal chains, after a split replacement when necessary. No Cat-hot equivalence or uniqueness theorem for the comparison is claimed.
references: Thomason1979, Theorem1.2; commentary Independence of the sequential homotopy type
notes: The assertion is complete on p.117; the following sentence continues in the next package, and its unfinished continuation is not invented here.

statement: For a strict fibred category C→T and a cofinal sequence t:N^op→T, put C_t=C×_T N^op; localization of its cartesian arrows gives the sequential colimit C_∞.
repair: The ordinary colimit is computed from the strict sequence of fibre categories.
notes: The sequence is cofinal in the preorder T_o; this is not automatically homotopy cofinal in T.

statement: The roof C←C_t→C_∞ yields an isomorphism in Hot if both legs are weak equivalences.
repair: Formal localization argument.
notes: The source is discussing a sufficient comparison mechanism; it does not rule out unrelated equivalences.

statement: For T=N^op, does the canonical localization C→colim_n C_n induce a weak equivalence?
repair: Yes. The comma-category proof in commentary p108 applies to every strict sequential diagram.
notes: Answered affirmatively in the following source paragraph.

statement: For every sequential system of small categories, the functor from its fibred Grothendieck construction over N^op to its ordinary colimit is a weak equivalence.
gap_or_error: The source announces conviction without giving the proof here.
repair: Complete finite-diagram contraction of every q/z is supplied in commentary p108.
notes: No injectivity or full-faithfulness assumption on transitions is needed.

statement: The preceding weak equivalence defines a morphism C_∞→C in Hot by the roof C_∞←C_t→C.
repair: Invert the horizontal weak equivalence in Hot.
notes: This does not define a functor C_∞→C in Cat.

statement: Is the canonical morphism C_∞→C always an isomorphism in Hot?
repair: No under the general hypotheses; take C=T=BG for a nontrivial group and a sequence constant on the identity. Then C_∞=* and the comparison is *→BG.
notes: The geometric all-arrows case is settled positively in §13, ms157–169.

statement: A cofiltered countably coinitial preorder T_o does not imply that BT is contractible.
repair: The one-object category BG has preorder a point and fundamental group G.
notes: The source supplies the one-object mechanism; the commentary specifies a nontrivial group.

statement: Under the homotopy hypothesis for parallel reindexings, C, C_∞ and the ind-object H_C have the same set of connected components.
repair: Connected components of the total category are the colimit of fibre components over T^op; the homotopy hypothesis factors this set-valued diagram through T_o^op, and a cofinal sequence computes that colimit.
notes: This statement retains no higher homotopy information.

statement: The total path category is provisionally considered dispensable except for its connected components.
repair: This is a working assessment, reversed by the strict path comparison in §13.
notes: Not a mathematical nonexistence theorem.

statement: Concatenation of all finite path types gives a strictly associative bifunctor on composable path categories, with empty paths as units.
repair: Follows from the strict concatenation formalism of §§7–9 and earlier VII-a commentary at ms48–53.
notes: The product is over the common endpoint; for based loops it is an ordinary product.

statement: A fixed colimit presentation C_∞ does not immediately supply a canonical associative composition, whereas the corresponding ind-objects have a composition in Ind Cat hot.
repair: Binary composition is constructed at ms125–127 using opposite padding conventions. For all arrows, §13 returns to strict all-types concatenation.
notes: The statement describes the stage of the construction, not an impossibility theorem.

statement: If T→T_o is smooth and coaspherical, or proper and aspherical, the desired base-change comparison C_t→C is a weak equivalence.
gap_or_error: No proof is reproduced on these pages; it uses the earlier base-change/asphericity results.
repair: Read as the sufficient criterion asserted using the preceding localizer calculus, not as a necessary condition.
notes: Smooth/proper are Grothendieck localizer notions; they are not ordinary categorical fibrations/cofibrations.

statement: The comparison is valid when T=T_o is a cofiltered preorder.
repair: A coinitial sequence is homotopy coinitial in the cofiltered preorder, and the fibred Grothendieck construction computes the appropriate homotopy colimit.
notes: The parallel-arrow obstruction vanishes in a preorder.

statement: The functor Ty→Ty_o is neither smooth nor proper, not even for the connectedness localizer.
gap_or_error: The assertion is stated without proof in the supplied source; the commentary supplies the explicit lifting-category calculation.
repair: Take S=Δ+Δ−Δ+ and T=Δ+. There are exactly two endpoint-preserving type maps S→T and both endomorphism monoids are trivial. Since T_o retains the same objects, both relevant lift categories are discrete two-point categories, hence not connected.
notes: This proves the source assertion without inferring failure of the geometric comparison from failure of a sufficient criterion.

statement: The comparison C_∞→Ch_Σ(X;a,b) is conjectured not to be a weak equivalence in general.
gap_or_error: The argument offered for the all-arrows loop case is false and withdrawn in footnote24.
repair: For Σ=Fl(X), §13 proves the comparison equivalence by the total path category. The argument here establishes no negative conclusion for general Σ.
notes: Do not extend the later all-arrows theorem to arbitrary relative categories without checking admissibility.

statement: The based loop object Ω(BX,a) cannot in general be modeled by a strictly associative simplicial monoid.
gap_or_error: Strict loop-group and Moore-loop models contradict the assertion.
repair: The source corrects itself in footnote24. Kan loop groups give a stronger simplicial-group model; Moore loops give strict associative topological monoids.
notes: The error is in the inference, not in the transcription.

statement: For a reduced simplicial set K, a simplicial group GK models Ω|K| and the unit K→Wbar GK is a weak equivalence.
repair: Kan’s loop-group theorem; verified in the modern proof by Stevenson.
notes: Footnote24 alludes to Quillen; the explicit reducedness hypothesis belongs in the modern statement.

statement: The fibre diagram descends through T_o^op to an ind-object H_T in Cat hot, and similarly after passage to Hot.
repair: Parallel reindexings are equal after taking natural-transformation homotopy classes; cofilteredness of T_o supplies the ind-index.
notes: H_T is not the ordinary colimit category.

statement: The stage maps define H_T→C_∞ in Ind Cat hot and Ind Hot, and a comparison C_∞→C only in Hot in general.
repair: The first map is the colimit cocone; the second is the roof of ms109.
notes: Keep the categories in which the different arrows live separate.

statement: The object of the finite-test presheaf category associated with C_∞ equals the filtered colimit of the stage-representable presheaves.
gap_or_error: Chapter V ms45 defines finite by finite objects and arrows, and ms51–52 defines Hot_0 using those categories. This does not imply homotopy compactness.
repair: Replace Hot_0 by homotopy-finite test types for this colimit formula; retain the separate valid finite-presentation formula in Cat hot.
notes: The source’s convention for finite tests must be stated explicitly.

statement: Concatenation gives functors Ch_{Σ,τ}(a,b)×Ch_{Σ,τ′}(b,c)→Ch_{Σ,ττ′}(a,c).
repair: Concatenate object diagrams and their endpoint-fixed natural transformations.
notes: The stage notation C_n×C_m→C_{n+m} applies to the chosen multiplicative power-type systems.

statement: The naive stage concatenations are compatible with the padding transition maps only up to categorical homotopy.
repair: The new constant blocks occur at different internal positions; the homotopy theorem identifies their reparametrizations in Cat hot.
notes: A homotopy-class compatibility is sufficient for the ind-object, but need not determine a coherent map between ordinary colimits.

statement: The ind-path objects form an associative category object in Ind Cat hot; if Σ=Fl(X), reversal supplies inverse morphisms and makes it a groupoid object.
repair: The finite-string localization calculus and the earlier homotopy theorem yield the unit, associativity and inverse identities.
references: Commentary p117; earlier III–V commentary ms27
notes: Inverses are identities in the localized homotopy category, not strict inverse paths in Cat.

statement: For a test object Y, define H_T^Y(a,b)=Hom_{Ind Cat hot}(Y,H_T(a,b)).
gap_or_error: The printed subscript Cat hot suppresses the ind-category when the target is an ind-object.
repair: Interpret the Hom in Ind Cat hot, using constant embedding for ordinary Y.
notes: For ind-Y the set is defined by the ind-Hom formula, not by an ordinary functor category X(Y).

statement: The sets H_T^Y(a,b), with object set Ob X, form a groupoid if Σ=Fl(X) and a category for a general Σ.
repair: Apply the representable functor Hom(Y,−), which preserves finite products, to the category/groupoid object.
notes: This is formal once the ind-composition laws are established.

statement: For ordinary Y, H_T^Y(a,b) is the Hom set between a_Y and b_Y in Fun(Y,X)[Σ_Y^{-1}], where Σ_Y consists of pointwise Σ natural transformations.
gap_or_error: The display on ms117 omits the superscript Y on H_T.
repair: Restore the superscript in the modern statement; finite localized zigzags impose one uniform stage bound over Y.
references: Commentary p117; earlier III–V commentary ms30–33
notes: The edition slip is retained in the source and recorded separately.

statement: C_∞(t) is said to be isomorphic in Hot for every cofinal sequence t, though initially without canonical isomorphisms.
gap_or_error: The general assertion cannot be inferred from the homotopy hypothesis alone; in particular the stated comparison morphisms need not be equivalences.
repair: The all-arrows path case has a later direct geometric proof. The FI^op example in commentary p121 disproves the general claim that every comparison map is invertible.
notes: The counterexample has abstractly isomorphic colimit objects, but a noninvertible canonical comparison; it directly refutes the morphism assertion.
